bruteforce_success.note: Password guessing from one public address ends in a successful login and immediate account creation.

webshell.note: Scanner enumeration followed by a 200 on an uploaded PHP path carrying a command parameter.

cron_persistence.note: A service account rewrites its crontab to pull a remote script and pipe it to a shell.

exfil_staging.note: Bulk archive written to /tmp on the customer database, then pushed outbound to a public address.

lateral_ssh.note: New authorized key on the database host followed by a key-based login from the web tier.

pkexec_privesc.note: Unprivileged web account fails sudo, then crashes a setuid helper in the way CVE-2021-4034 does.

apt_upgrade_fim.note: A burst of integrity changes confined to package-managed paths during a scheduled upgrade window.

admin_maintenance.note: Named administrator on an internal address running a package upgrade during working hours.

internet_noise.note: Untargeted credential guessing from scattered addresses against an internet-facing host, none successful.

backup_failure.note: A backup job failing the same way it fails every night. An operational fault, not a security event.

scanner_404s.note: Commodity scanner sweeping known paths. Every response is a 404 and nothing follows.

build_churn.note: Continuous integration workspace churn on a host whose entire job is creating and deleting files.

offhours_login.note: A real account authenticating from an unfamiliar public address at 01:03, with nothing before or after it.

offhours_useradd.note: Account creation at 02:03 with no session, no sudo, and no provisioning context in the data.

reverse_shell.note: A web service account spawns bash with a network redirection to an external host.

shadow_read.note: A non-root service account reads /etc/shadow on the domain controller.

log_tamper.note: Authentication logs are truncated shortly after a privileged session, hiding activity.

payload_download_exec.note: A remote binary is fetched to /tmp, made executable, and run within seconds.

systemd_persistence.note: A new systemd service unit is written that launches a script from /tmp on boot.

dns_tunnel.note: Sustained high-volume TXT lookups to a single external domain, consistent with DNS tunnelling.

mass_encrypt.note: Thousands of files renamed with a new extension in minutes on the database host.

vpn_bruteforce_success.note: A run of failed VPN authentications from one address ends in a success at 00:24.

mail_relay_abuse.note: An authenticated account sends thousands of messages to external recipients in minutes.

sudoers_backdoor.note: A NOPASSWD entry for a freshly created account is written into /etc/sudoers.d.

certbot_renewal.note: Certificate files change under /etc/letsencrypt during the scheduled renewal window.

logrotate.note: Log files rotate and shrink at 00:03; the size reduction is logrotate, not tampering.

apt_remove.note: A package is removed and its files deleted during a scheduled maintenance window.

ansible_run.note: Config management pushes a batch of file changes from the automation host during business hours.

dev_git_push.note: A developer on the office network authenticates and runs git operations on the build host.

backup_cron_ok.note: The nightly backup job runs, writes an archive, and exits zero. Expected operations.

docker_pull.note: Image layers are written under /var/lib/docker during a normal build pull.

kernel_upgrade.note: Boot files change during a kernel package upgrade, alongside the dpkg record that explains them.

service_crashloop.note: A mail service crashes and is restarted repeatedly. An availability fault, not an attacker.

monitoring_probe.note: A monitoring system health-checks an endpoint on a fixed interval from the internal poller.

offhours_dbdump.note: A full database dump runs at 02:36 by a service account with no scheduled job visible for it.

sudo_group_add.note: An existing account is added to the sudo group with no change ticket or session context in the data.

new_geo_login.note: A valid account authenticates from a country it has never connected from before, nothing else attached.

single_binary_change.note: One system binary changes checksum with no package-manager record in the same window to explain it.

dormant_login.note: An account dormant for months authenticates successfully at 01:36; unusual but not proof of misuse.

encoded_command.note: A base64-encoded shell command runs under an admin session; could be tooling or an attempt to hide intent.
